subject: chemistry
name: Chemistry
review_note: Draft written for Quark. Grade levels are typical North American placements and vary by curriculum. Needs review by a subject teacher before it is treated as authoritative.

topics.name: Properties of materials
learning_goals: Describe and sort materials by properties such as hardness, flexibility and whether they float.
Choose materials for a purpose.

misconceptions.description: States a guess as an observation.
misconceptions.example: 'It is made of plastic' after only looking at its colour.

misconceptions.description: Uses a vague property word.

example_problems.prompt: Why are windows made of glass?
example_problems.answer: Glass is transparent, so light passes through

topics.name: States of matter and changes of state
learning_goals: Describe solids, liquids and gases.
Explain melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation and boiling.
key_concepts: Heating and cooling cause changes of state

misconceptions.description: Thinks mass changes when a substance changes state.
misconceptions.example: 'Ice weighs more than the water it melts into.'

misconceptions.description: Thinks the bubbles in boiling water are air.

example_problems.prompt: What is the change of state when water vapour forms droplets on a cold glass?

topics.name: Mixtures, solutions and separation
learning_goals: Distinguish pure substances, mixtures and solutions.
Choose separation methods such as filtering, evaporation and distillation.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a dissolved solid has disappeared.
misconceptions.example: 'The sugar is gone, so the mass went down.'

misconceptions.description: Chooses a method that cannot separate the mixture.
misconceptions.example: Filters salt water to get salt.

example_problems.prompt: How would you get salt back from salt water?

topics.name: Particle model of matter
learning_goals: Use the particle model to explain states, diffusion and expansion.
Relate particle motion to temperature.

misconceptions.description: Gives particles the bulk properties of the substance.
Thinks there is air between particles.
misconceptions.example: 'Air fills the gaps between water particles.'

example_problems.prompt: Why does a balloon get bigger when warmed?
example_problems.answer: The gas particles move faster and hit the walls harder and more often, pushing the balloon out

topics.name: Physical and chemical changes
learning_goals: Tell physical changes from chemical changes.
Use evidence of a chemical change: gas, colour, precipitate, energy.

misconceptions.description: Treats any change of appearance as chemical.
misconceptions.example: 'Melting ice is a chemical change because it looks different.'

misconceptions.description: Thinks burning destroys matter.
misconceptions.example: 'When wood burns the mass is destroyed.'

example_problems.prompt: Is rusting a physical or chemical change? Why?
example_problems.answer: Chemical: a new substance (iron oxide) forms

topics.name: Atomic structure and the periodic table
learning_goals: Describe protons, neutrons and electrons and draw Bohr-Rutherford diagrams.
Use the periodic table to find atomic number, mass and trends.

misconceptions.description: Uses mass number as the number of electrons.
Gets the number of valence electrons wrong for a group.

example_problems.prompt: How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in a neutral atom of oxygen-16?

topics.name: Balancing equations and conservation of mass
learning_goals: Write word and skeleton equations.
Balance chemical equations using coefficients.

misconceptions.description: Changes subscripts to balance.
Writes diatomic elements as single atoms.

example_problems.prompt: Balance: __ Fe + __ O2 -> __ Fe2O3
Balance: __ CH4 + __ O2 -> __ CO2 + __ H2O

topics.name: Ionic and covalent bonding
learning_goals: Explain ionic and covalent bonding.
Draw Lewis structures and predict properties from bond type.

misconceptions.description: Describes an ionic compound as separate molecules.
Miscounts total valence electrons in a Lewis structure.

example_problems.prompt: What type of bond forms between magnesium and chlorine? Write the formula.

topics.name: Chemical names and formulas
learning_goals: Name and write formulas for ionic and molecular compounds, including polyatomic ions.
Use the criss-cross method correctly.

misconceptions.description: Does not balance charges.
Uses prefixes for ionic compounds.

example_problems.prompt: Write the formula for aluminium oxide.
Name CuSO4.

topics.name: Types of chemical reactions
learning_goals: Classify reactions as synthesis, decomposition, single and double displacement, combustion and neutralization.
Predict products of simple reactions.

misconceptions.description: Predicts products for the wrong reaction type.
Forgets water as a product of complete combustion.

example_problems.prompt: Classify: 2 KClO3 -> 2 KCl + 3 O2

topics.name: Acids, bases and pH
learning_goals: Describe properties of acids and bases and use the pH scale.
Write neutralization reactions and (later) calculate pH.
key_concepts: Neutralization forms a salt and water

misconceptions.description: Confuses strong with concentrated.
Takes the log without the negative sign.

example_problems.prompt: What is the pH of a solution with [H+] = 1 x 10^-4 mol/L?

topics.name: The mole and molar mass
learning_goals: Use the mole to count particles.
Convert between mass, moles and number of particles.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a mole is a mass.
Miscalculates molar mass by missing a subscript.

example_problems.prompt: How many moles are in 36 g of water (M = 18.02 g/mol)?

topics.name: Stoichiometry and limiting reagents
learning_goals: Use mole ratios from balanced equations to calculate amounts.
Identify the limiting reagent and calculate theoretical and percent yield.

misconceptions.description: Uses a mass ratio instead of a mole ratio.
misconceptions.example: Uses grams directly in the equation's coefficients

misconceptions.description: Calculates yield from the reagent in excess.
misconceptions.example: Uses the larger amount to find product mass

example_problems.prompt: 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O. How many moles of water form from 3 mol of H2 with excess O2?

topics.name: Solution concentration and dilution
learning_goals: Calculate molar concentration.
Use C1V1 = C2V2 for dilutions.

misconceptions.description: Uses millilitres in c = n / V.
Uses C1V1 = C2V2 when there is a reaction, not a dilution.
misconceptions.example: Titration solved with C1V1 = C2V2 for a 1:2 ratio

example_problems.prompt: What is the concentration of 0.25 mol of NaCl in 500 mL of solution?

topics.name: Gas laws
learning_goals: Use Boyle's, Charles's and combined gas laws and the ideal gas law PV = nRT.
Explain gas behaviour with kinetic molecular theory.

misconceptions.description: Uses degrees Celsius in a gas law.
misconceptions.example: V2 = V1 x 40/20 for 20 to 40 degrees C

misconceptions.description: Uses the wrong value of R for the units.

example_problems.prompt: A gas occupies 2.0 L at 300 K. What volume at 450 K at constant pressure?

topics.name: Energy changes in reactions
learning_goals: Describe exothermic and endothermic reactions.
Calculate enthalpy changes using q = mc(delta T), Hess's law or bond energies.

misconceptions.description: Gives an exothermic reaction a positive delta H.
Thinks breaking bonds releases energy.
misconceptions.example: 'Energy is released when the bonds break.'

example_problems.prompt: 100 g of water warms by 5.0 degrees C (c = 4.18 J/g C). How much energy did it absorb?

topics.name: Reaction rates
learning_goals: Explain how temperature, concentration, surface area and catalysts affect rate.
Use collision theory.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a catalyst is used up or changes the products.
misconceptions.example: 'The catalyst becomes part of the product.'

misconceptions.description: States the effect without the collision-theory reason.

example_problems.prompt: Why does powdered zinc react faster with acid than a lump of zinc?
example_problems.answer: Larger surface area gives more collisions per second

topics.name: Intermolecular forces and properties
learning_goals: Identify dispersion, dipole-dipole and hydrogen bonding forces.
Relate them to boiling point and solubility.

misconceptions.description: Thinks covalent bonds break when a molecular substance boils.
misconceptions.example: 'Water boils when the O-H bonds break.'

misconceptions.description: Calls any H-containing molecule hydrogen-bonded.

example_problems.prompt: Why does water have a much higher boiling point than methane?
example_problems.answer: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds; methane has only weak dispersion forces

topics.name: Organic chemistry basics
learning_goals: Name simple hydrocarbons and functional groups.
Draw structural formulas and isomers.

misconceptions.description: Numbers the main chain from the wrong end.
Gives carbon more or fewer than four bonds.

example_problems.prompt: Name CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3.

topics.name: Chemical equilibrium
learning_goals: Describe dynamic equilibrium and write equilibrium expressions.
Use Le Chatelier's principle to predict shifts.

misconceptions.description: Thinks reactions stop at equilibrium.
Includes solids or liquids in K.

example_problems.prompt: For N2 + 3 H2 <-> 2 NH3 (exothermic), which way does it shift if temperature rises?
